sentences.text: Petitioner has filed this petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioner case is as Follows:
That on 28.09.2022 at about 04.00 AM., petitioner was traveling as a passenger in Tempo Traveler bearing reg. No.KA-02-AF-2366, towards K.R. Puram in outer ring road, near Karthik nagar junction, Bangalore, where in the driver of Truck bearing reg No.KA-53-B-1824 has parked his vehicle on the right side of the road, negligently without putting any signals for his vehicle.
Driver of the tempo traveler bearing No.KA-02-AF-2366 dashed against the said parked trucke and caused accident.
In the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Petitioner took first aid at Jeevika Hospital and later he was shifted to Jain hospital, wherein he took treatment for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

In total he has spent Rs.1,00,000/-
for his medical expenses.
According to the petitioner Respondent no.2 is the owner of Truck and he insured his vehicle with the respondent no.1.

Further respondent no.4 is the owner of the Tempo and he insured his vehicle with the respondent no.3.
3.
Petitioner stated that he is 22 years of age working as a software engineer and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month, and his family is depend on his income.

He stated that accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the drivers of the Truck and tempo and the policy of the said vehicles was in force and they are liable to pay the compensation amount.

Further he stated that the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.83/2022 against both the vehicles and their drivers for Shreyas Hebbar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87234437/

He prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, respondent No.1,3 appeared through their counsel and filed vakalath and written statement by denying the entire petition averments.
Respondent No.2 and 4 does not chose to contest the petition, and they placed exparte.

5. Respondent no.1 contended that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of Tempo which belongs to respondent no.4 and he is liable to pay the compensation amount and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.

6. Respondent no.3 contended that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of Truck which belongs to respondent no.2 and he is liable to pay the compensation amount and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
7. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 produced and marked 13 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 13 and he is fully cross examined.
Respondent no.1 and 3 examined RW.1 and 2 and they are fully cross examined.

9. On the basis of pleadings I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 28.09.2022 at 04.00 AM., at Karthiknagar junction, outer ring road, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Truck bearing Reg No.KA-53-B-1824, when he was traveling as a passenger in tempo traveler bearing No.KA-02-AF-2366 as alleged in the petition?.

2.Whether respondent No.3 proves that the driver of the tempo bearing No.KA-02-AF-2366 was not having effective valid driving license as on the date of Shreyas Hebbar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87234437/
3 accident and he has violated the policy condition and accident occurred due to his negligence?
3.Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

sentences.text:
if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4.What order or award?
10.
PW1 being the the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, mahazar, IMV report, Final report, wound certificate which are at Ex.P.1 to 5 & 13.
12.

On careful perusal of the same it is evident that one Umesh s/o Bore Gowda was the driver of Truck bearing reg No.KA-53-B-1824 and one Moganna Gowda S/o Nanje Gowda was driver of the Tempo bearing reg No.KA-02-AF-2366.
It is also true from the final report that the driver of the tempo has pleaded guilty and he is convicted.
The final report filed by the investigating officer which is at Ex.P5, where in jurisdictional police have registered the case against the drivers of the both the vehicles involved in the accident.
The aforesaid facts establishes the involvement of the aforesaid vehicles and its drivers acts in the accident.
In the cross examination of PW-1 he has not specifically deposed which driver of the vehicle was rash and negligent as on the date of the incident.
Respondent No.1 and 2 have not placed the evidence to show that the said Truck was being used for the metro work which was in progress at the place of accident.
Respondent No.1 and 3 have not chosen to examine the IO of the case, further they have failed to probabilise the contention as taken by them in their respective written statement 13.
Accordingly involvement of both the vehicles and the negligent act of the drivers based on the police records can not be doubted.
The police records are not disputed nor denied by the respondent No.1 and 3 and they remained un-impeached and un-rebutted.
14. Ex.P13 is the is the wound certificate, Ex.P6 to 10 are the bills.
The aforesaid undisputed documents reveals that petitioner has sustained bleeding injury to his nose and and abrasion on the right side of his face in the said accident.

Ex.P.6 to 10 are the medical bills, it shows that petitioner Shreyas Hebbar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87234437/
4 has incurred medical expenses of Rs.8,259/-.
15.

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, Medicines,
Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
16.
Petitioner took treatment at Mahaveer Jain hospital, Bangalore.
He has tendered the wound certificate, on perusal of the same it is apparent that, he has incurred Rs.8,259/- towards actual medical expenses.
Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the medical bills.
Accordingly the wound certificate, and the medical bills issued form the hospital has to be accepted.

Admittedly he has not taken treatment as in patient, for transportation, nourishing food,
he might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore in addition to the actual medical expenses of Rs.8,259/-, I award Rs.2,000/-.
In total petitioner is entitled for Rs.10,259/- compensation under this head.

Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
17.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained on his nose and abrasion on his face.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries he has forgone certain amenities available for him.
There fore I award Rs.2000/- under these conventional heads.
18. Except the aforesaid heads petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.

In all petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
1
Pecuniary damages Rs.10,259/- 3 Non pecuniary damages Rs. 2,000/- 4 TOTAL Rs.12,259/-
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.12,259/- only.
19. Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% P.A.

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
The insurance company that is respondent no.1 and 3 have not disputed the validity of the policy issued to the said vehicles involved in the accident.

Apparently the driver of the Truck which belongs to respondent No.2 has not taken precautionary measure by putting the signal lights for the Truck while parking the same in the road for the alleged metro work.
AS per the police records, the truck driver has parked the vehicle on the road and thereby he has abstracted the vehicle movements.

On the other hand as per the entry in final report the driver of the tempo which belongs to respondent No.4 has admitted his guilt and thereby he is Shreyas Hebbar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87234437/
5 convicted.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 and 3 have failed to establish their contention that the owners of the said vehicles has violated the policy conditions.

Evidently the drivers of aforesaid vehicles have contributed their rash and negligent acts which is the cause for the accident and as as result of which petitioner sustained the injury in the accident.
Accordingly both are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Out of the compensation amount respondent No.3 being the insurer of the tempo has to pay 75% of the compensation amount and respondent No.1 being the insurer of Truck has to pay Rs.25% of the compensation amount.

Accordingly Respondent No. 1 and 3 are liable to pay the compensation amount as stated above and they are directed to deposit the same with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

The authorities relied on by the counsel appearing for respondent No.3 as stated at aforesaid para 8 (1 to 4), wherein concept of assessing the contributory negligence and fixing of liability is dealt with.

With great respect to the aforesaid authorities and by considering the principles laid down therein and with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, I am answering Issue No.1 to 3 in the partly affirmative.
21. Issue No.4:

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.12,259/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent no.1 and 3 are directed to deposit 75% and 25% of the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, office is directed to release the entire amount to the petitioner through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed off.
Draw award accordingly.
